Abstract
Mapless autonomous navigation in unknown multi-obstacle environments remains challenging for deep reinforcement learning due to limited perception, sparse rewards, and distribution shifts between training and deployment scenarios. Existing methods mainly rely on instantaneous observations or individual enhancement strategies, which often struggle to balance exploration robustness and navigation efficiency. This paper proposes a Curriculum Learning and Intrinsic Curiosity-enhanced Temporal Proximal Policy Optimization framework, referred to as CLI-PPO, for end-to-end autonomous navigation. The framework integrates temporal state representation, intrinsic exploration, and progressive task scheduling into PPO, where an LSTM network improves sequential decision-making under partial observability, an Intrinsic Curiosity Module enhances exploration in unfamiliar regions, and Curriculum Learning stabilizes policy optimization by gradually increasing task difficulty. A hybrid reward function combining target guidance, obstacle avoidance, and exploration incentives is designed for policy training. 4. Discussion
The experiments show that the three components influence different stages of the navigation process. The original in-distribution evaluation and the repeated training runs describe overall policy performance and variation between runs, while the structured distribution-shift and perturbation tests examine how the learned behavior changes when obstacle geometry, density, sensing, or command execution is altered. Temporal memory mainly affects how successive observations are incorporated into motion decisions; ICM changes the transitions explored during training; and Curriculum Learning determines how task difficulty is introduced. These differences lead to distinct performance patterns in success rate, return, path efficiency, and collision avoidance across the tested conditions.
The recurrent policy processes a sequence of observations rather than an isolated measurement at each decision step. PPO+LSTM and CLI-PPO both reach the

[... bounded source excerpt ...]

ces different advantages across navigation conditions rather than the same improvement in every environment and metric.
5. Conclusions
This work presents CLI-PPO, a navigation framework that integrates temporal observation processing, action-conditioned curiosity, and progressive task training for unknown multi-obstacle environments. The hybrid reward function combines target guidance, obstacle avoidance, and exploration-related feedback during policy learning.
The experiments show that temporal representation, intrinsic exploration, and curriculum-based task scheduling affect different aspects of mapless navigation. PPO+ICM+ Curriculum achieves higher mean success rates and Euclidean-reference SPL across the tested obstacle-density conditions. CLI-PPO obtains higher cumulative returns, smaller observed success-rate deviations across the repeated training runs, and shorter completion times in the two selected structured distribution-shift scenarios.
